statement: For every positive integer m not in {1,4,5,6,7}, define L(m) and A(m) as in problem.md. If 11 does not divide m, then L(m)=2/11; for r=m mod 11, A(m)={4/11,7/11} when r is 2 or 9, A(m)={5/11,6/11} when r is 3 or 8, and A(m)={4/11,5/11,6/11,7/11} when r is in {1,4,5,6,7,10}. At m=11, L=2/13 and A={4/13,9/13}. At m=22, L=2/13 and A={4/13,6/13,7/13,9/13}. If m=11n with n>=3, then L(m)=2n/(11n+4) and A(m)={(5n+2)/(11n+4),(6n+2)/(11n+4)}. Consequently, the parameters satisfying the strict inequalities 1/7<L(m)<1/6 are exactly {11,22,33}.
contribution: A complete elementary resolution of the source-derived one-parameter family, including every equality time and the strict near-tight classification. The proof replaces finite pattern fitting by an exact superlevel-set decomposition for the base quintuple and uniform endpoint inequalities for all multiples of 11. The inspected primary source reports m=22 and m=33 but does not give this family theorem; priority beyond the searched source is not asserted.
